evidence.claim: The official PMO biography states that Narendra Modi served as Prime Minister from 2019 to 2024, so he was in office throughout 2022.
evidence.title: Know the PM
evidence.excerpt: The official PMO biography states that Narendra Modi served as Prime Minister from 2019 to 2024, so he was in office throughout 2022.
evidence.source_locator: biography paragraph with the service dates
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government biography; direct office-tenure claim.
evidence.period_fit: Confirms officeholding during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributes executive office to Modi, but not any specific nuclear decision.
contrary_evidence: Promotional tone and no detail on nuclear authority or 2022 conduct.

evidence.claim: The Supreme Court-appointed Pegasus panel found no conclusive evidence on the devices it examined, but the Chief Justice said the central government had not cooperated with the probe.
evidence.title: No evidence, Govt didn’t cooperate: SC panel on Pegasus
evidence.excerpt: The Supreme Court-appointed Pegasus panel found no conclusive evidence on the devices it examined, but the Chief Justice said the central government had not cooperated with the probe.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting of the Supreme Court’s summary of the panel report; reliable for the non-cooperation finding, limited by the panel’s inability to reach conclusive technical proof.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period oversight and surveillance evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi-led central government as the entity that did not cooperate with the court-appointed probe.
contrary_evidence: The panel did not find conclusive proof of Pegasus use on the devices it examined.
That makes the allegation unresolved rather than proven in this source alone.

evidence.claim: HRW said the Indian government was harassing the Centre for Promotion of Social Concerns and People’s Watch, including through CBI action under the foreign-funding law, as part of a wider crackdown on civil society.
evidence.title: India Should Stop Using Abusive Foreign Funding Law
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the Indian government was harassing the Centre for Promotion of Social Concerns and People’s Watch, including through CBI action under the foreign-funding law, as part of a wider crackdown on civil society.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed human-rights reporting with named organizations, dated events, and explicit attribution to the Indian government.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period for early 2022 and squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct central-government attribution through the CBI/FCRA apparatus under Modi’s administration.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the case as fraud and foreign-funding compliance enforcement.
The report is advocacy-oriented, so its characterization of motive is not itself a legal finding.

evidence.claim: The 2022 country report says the Kashmir Press Club was forcibly taken over in January by people allegedly close to local administration, and that new accreditation rules could suspend journalists for work deemed harmful to sovereignty or national security.
evidence.title: India
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 country report says the Kashmir Press Club was forcibly taken over in January by people allegedly close to local administration, and that new accreditation rules could suspend journalists for work deemed harmful to sovereignty or national security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Institutional journalism research with explicit 2022 country findings; strong for media-environment context, though the survey portion is not nationally representative.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is partly direct and partly indirect: the central ministry issued the accreditation rules, while the takeover involved local administration and armed police.
contrary_evidence: The report is partly survey-based and limited to English-speaking online users for some metrics.
The Kashmir Press Club episode involves alleged local-administration proximity rather than a court-tested national order.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that BJP leaders instructed officials to be extremely cautious about religious remarks after Prophet-related comments triggered protests, and said Muslims were under pressure on worship and hijab issues.
evidence.title: India's ruling party asks officials to exercise caution on religious issues after Islamic nations protest
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that BJP leaders instructed officials to be extremely cautious about religious remarks after Prophet-related comments triggered protests, and said Muslims were under pressure on worship and hijab issues.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on party instructions and the surrounding backlash; strong for the reported directive, weaker for broader causal interpretation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Party-level attribution is direct to the BJP, and indirectly to Modi as the party’s national leader and government head.
contrary_evidence: The instruction was framed as cautionary messaging rather than overt repression.
It does not by itself prove direct Modi personal authorship of the remarks.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the government sought to calm anger at home and abroad after ruling-party remarks on the Prophet, and that 38 people were arrested for rioting in one northern city.
evidence.title: India rushes to quell outrage after insulting remarks on Islam
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the government sought to calm anger at home and abroad after ruling-party remarks on the Prophet, and that 38 people were arrested for rioting in one northern city.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated contemporaneous reporting with a concrete arrest count and direct government response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution is direct to the Modi administration; the triggering remarks were by BJP officials rather than Modi himself.
contrary_evidence: The government response was calm-down and damage control, not open endorsement of violence.
The arrests were local-law-enforcement actions rather than a national decree.

evidence.claim: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting used emergency powers under the IT Rules to block 16 YouTube news channels and one Facebook account, saying they spread fake news on security, foreign relations, communal harmony, and public order.
evidence.title: Ministry of I&B blocks 16 YouTube news channels for spreading disinformation related to India’s national security, foreign relations and public order
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting used emergency powers under the IT Rules to block 16 YouTube news channels and one Facebook account, saying they spread fake news on security, foreign relations, communal harmony, and public order.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official release with a precise date, concrete blocking action, and the government’s stated justification.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct central-government attribution under the Modi administration through the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the action as anti-disinformation and public-order protection.
The source itself does not prove the blocked content was genuinely disinformation.

unresolved_gaps: No public 2022 evidence of a Modi-directed command-and-control reform, custody audit, launch-readiness change, or internal NCA practice change.
Personal attribution is thin for the more favorable multilateral statements and nuclear-governance positions.
The Russia balancing record is mostly government-level and UN-mission level rather than a clearly documented personal decision by Modi on oil, abstentions, or summit sequencing.
There is no 2022 external-combat or proxy-war exposure to test civilian-protection or proxy-control lenses in a strong way.
Direct Modi-level incitement evidence is thinner than the broader BJP and state-level abuse record.
The strongest custody-death and abuse claims still rely on NGO and U.S. State Department reporting with mixed central/state attribution.
Direct evidence of Modi personally directing electoral manipulation is thin relative to the stronger party-level and institutional record.
Several items show contestability and oversight but do not themselves prove that Modi strengthened democratic institutions in 2022.
Household-level and median-welfare evidence is thinner than the macro, capex, and program-count evidence.
Corruption, favoritism, and politically connected business privilege are underdeveloped relative to investment and growth material.
Independent outcome measures and subnational equity checks are still thin relative to the many ministry self-reports.
The current record is strong on inputs and service counts but weak on durable quality, learning, nutrition, and sustained poverty improvement.
No audited evidence of direct personal falsehood, correction, or hidden conflicts of interest has been recovered for 2022.
The negative items are mostly institutional opacity or noncooperation, not direct proof of personal self-dealing or a documented lie by Modi.
Project-level outcome audits and durability checks are still thinner than the program-design and rollout material.
Direct evidence that Modi replaced a specific ineffective implementer is absent.
